request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a contact. It's stored trimmed and lower-cased, shown on each row, and refused if another person on the sheet already has it. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**Stored data**
- New migration `V51__person_contact.sql` adds a `contact` column to both `person` and `person_history`. It drops and recreates the history trigger around the change, the same way earlier migrations do.
- Duplicate contacts are refused in the server code, not by a database constraint.

**Server**
- `ValidatePerson` trims and lower-cases the contact; a blank one is stored as none.
- `AddPerson` and `ApplyPerson` refuse a contact that another person already has, with "The contact is already in use." Nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
- In an edit, the existing version check runs first and the contact check after it.
- The contact is carried through `Person`, `PersonRequest`, `PersonResponse` and `People` (read, insert and update). `contactTaken` is the new lookup.
- `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<c>` when one was given. `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<c>` when it changed, and `contact=` when it was cleared.

**Front end**
- The person form has a contact input (`person-form-contact`), filled when the editor opens and cleared after an add.
- Each row has a contact cell (`person-contact`).

**One fix along the way:** my first version also checked for duplicates in the browser. That made one step fail. In the test, uma had Cam's editor open while vic saved a change to Cam. The browser check then refused uma's save before it reached the server, so the form never reloaded Cam's current version, and uma's next save was rejected as a conflict. I removed the browser check, so the server alone decides.
